--White-2 is another paint style named White (#FFF); --White is not used here: they are two styles, keep each where the layer names it.
#FFF is written raw 4 times (background of 1:3, background of 1:7, background of 2:3) and equals --White-2: use the token.
#F00 is written raw 4 times (background of 1:4, border of 1:7, background of 2:4) and equals --Accent: use the token.
4 layers keep Figma's default names (1:2 "Frame 12", 1:4 "Rectangle 7", 2:2 "Frame 12", …): name the elements by their role in the code.

4 frames have no auto layout, so their children are placed absolutely (1:2 "Frame 12" with 2 children, Figma reads it as display: flex; flex-direction: column; padding: 10px 0 0 10px; align-items: center; gap: 8px; 2:2 "Frame 12" with 2 children, Figma reads it as display: flex; flex-direction: column; padding: 10px 0 0 10px; align-items: center; gap: 8px; 1:22 "Dots" with 3 children; and 1 more): build them as a flow if they are meant to resize.
2 rectangles cover their parents under the content (1:3 "Backdrop" covers 1:2 "Frame 12"; 2:3 "Backdrop" covers 2:2 "Frame 12"): write each as its parent's background, not as an element.
2 frames only wrap one layer (1:5 "Wrapper" only wraps 1:6; 2:5 "Wrapper" only wraps 2:6): they may not need elements of their own.

6 texts or content frames have a fixed width narrower than their column (1:5 "Wrapper" 200px wide in 400px; 2:5 "Wrapper" 200px wide in 400px; 1:26 "Body" 240px wide in 400px; and 3 more): use fill + max-width, so it follows the column.

line-height normal is Figma's Auto line height: the font's own spacing, about 1.2× the font size for most fonts (1:6 "Note"; I1:9;2:1 "Label"; 2:6 "Note"; and 7 more); where the build must match to the pixel, read with autoLineHeight: "px", which writes the px Figma renders where the read can tell (a text that hugs its lines shows it for its font and size).

is a line break inside a paragraph (Shift+Enter in Figma,
in HTML), not spaces (1:6 "Note"; 2:6 "Note").

2 layers have strokes centred on their edges (1:7 "Card"; 2:7 "Card"): Figma paints half of it outside the box, a CSS border all inside; where it must match to the pixel, use an outline with outline-offset of minus half its width.
2 frames were detached from a component (1:8 "Detached card"; 2:8 "Detached card"): check whether the component fits instead.

2 layers are wider or taller than the room their auto layout parent gives them, so they overflow it in Figma too (1:8 "Detached card" 500px wide in 400px; 2:8 "Detached card" 500px wide in 400px): decide whether the build wraps, clips or lets them out.
4 empty layers space the flow (1:8 "Detached card" 500px × 60px; 2:8 "Detached card" 500px × 60px; 1:19 "Gap" 24px × 40px; and 1 more): use the parent's gap or padding, not an element.

2 layers inside instances differ from their component outside its properties (I1:9;2:1 "Label": color; I2:9;2:1 "Label": color): give the component a property or a variant for them, or build them as one-offs.

2 auto layout frames place children absolutely (1:13 "Stack by hand": 3 children are placed absolutely inside an auto layout parent, likely a stack with gap 10px; 2:13 "Stack by hand": 3 children are placed absolutely inside an auto layout parent, likely a stack with gap 10px): the design shows the look, not the build; put them in the flow, with that gap where there is one.
2 texts break their lines by hand and hug them (1:21 "Title"; 2:21 "Title"): unless a break is meant, let the build wrap the text in its width.
2 frames without auto layout space their children evenly (1:22 "Dots": gap 10px; 2:22 "Dots": gap 10px): build them as a flow with that gap.
2 frames of fixed height clip their content (1:27 "Excerpt" 40px tall cuts 1:28; 2:27 "Excerpt" 40px tall cuts 2:28): let the height follow the content, or decide how the build cuts it.
2 structures are built 3 times or more without a component (4:1 "Plan" and 2 alike; 5:1 "Tag" and 2 alike): build each as one component and use instances.

2 sets of top-level frames of one size share most of their layers (1:31 "Pricing" and 2:31 "Pricing" share most of their layers; 1:37 "Menu" and 2:37 "Menu" share most of their layers): they look like states of one component; build it once, with variants.
2 layers bake fades into images (1:29 "Hero"; 2:29 "Hero"): an export flattens the fade and stretches it with the box; export the raw image with original: true and rebuild the gradient in CSS.

2 layers are filled with tiled textures (1:30 "Grain" tiled at 0.5×; 2:30 "Grain" tiled at 0.5×): a texture renders coarser or finer at another scale; export one tile at the scale given and repeat it.
Fonts missing on this machine (Inter) in I1:9;2:1 "Label", I2:9;2:1 "Label": Figma could not lay these texts out, so their sizes may be off.
gap 16px on 2 layers (1:10 "Stack"; 2:10 "Stack") matches --space-16, Figma's own match for that field: use the token.
